hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.

hindi: बहुत बड़े धन के लिए भी कोई अपने शरीर का नाश नहीं चाहेगा।
english: Even for a very great gain, no one would wish for the destruction of his body.

hindi: और दण्ड की कठोरता से वह वही दोष दूसरों से प्राप्त करता है।
english: And through harshness of punishment he incurs that very evil from others.
notes: 'tam eva doṣam' = the same evil just named in 35, destruction of the body.

hindi: इस प्रकार क्रोध से उत्पन्न तीन का वर्ग है।
english: Thus the set of three born of anger.

hindi: काम से उत्पन्न तो मृगया, द्यूत, स्त्रियाँ और पान — यह चार का वर्ग है।
english: The one born of desire, on the other hand, is the set of four: hunting, gambling, women and drink.

hindi: उसमें, "मृगया और द्यूत में मृगया अधिक भारी है" — ऐसा पिशुन कहते हैं।
english: Of that, "between hunting and gambling, hunting is the more serious," says Pishuna.
notes: 'tasya' = of that set of four; the comparison of its members begins here.

words.gloss: fear of robbers, enemies, wild beasts, forest fire and stumbling, and loss of direction
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva (last members bhaya, diṅ-moha)

hindi: "उसमें चोर, शत्रु, हिंसक पशु, दावानल और फिसलने का भय, दिशा-भ्रम, तथा भूख और प्यास — ये प्राणों के लिए बाधा हैं।
english: "In it there is danger to life: fear of robbers, enemies, wild beasts, forest fire and stumbling, loss of direction, and hunger and thirst.
notes: 'din' is the e-text's spelling of diś before m (diṅ-moha, 'confusion of directions'); not a typo. The long compound can also be read as a plain dvandva with 'bhaya' as a separate item ('fear'); the reading here takes the first five members as the objects of 'bhaya'. 'prāṇa-ābādhaḥ' singular predicate with plural subjects.

hindi: द्यूत में तो पासों का ज्ञाता जीतता ही है, जैसे जयत्सेन और दुर्योधन ने जीता" — ऐसा कहा गया है।
english: In gambling, on the other hand, one who knows dice simply wins, as (was won) by Jayatsena and Duryodhana." So it is said.
notes: 'jitam' impersonal passive: 'it is won by the dice-expert'. The two names are given as examples of winning; the text says nothing more about them.

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.

text_flags.why: 'ity' is the sandhi form of iti before a vowel, but the next word begins with k; the parallel lines 34, 52 and 58 read 'na-iti'. Possible typo in the e-text.

words.gloss: defeat of one or the other

hindi: उन दोनों में भी किसी एक की पराजय होती ही है — यह नल और युधिष्ठिर से समझाया जा चुका है।
english: Even of those two there is the defeat of one or the other; that is illustrated by Nala and Yudhishthira.
notes: 'tayoḥ' = of the two (dice-experts) who gamble, or of the two named in 41; the Sanskrit does not fix it.

hindi: वही जीता हुआ द्रव्य चारा बन जाता है, और वैर की परम्परा चलती रहती है।
english: That very property won (at play) is a bait, and (there is) a continuation of enmity.

words.gloss: by holding urine and faeces, hunger and the like

hindi: विद्यमान धन की हानि, अविद्यमान धन का अर्जन, बिना भोगे ही धन का नाश, तथा मल-मूत्र रोकने और भूख आदि से रोग की प्राप्ति — ये द्यूत के दोष हैं।
english: Loss of wealth one has, acquisition of wealth that is not real, loss of wealth before it is enjoyed, and contracting disease through holding urine and faeces, hunger and the like: these are the evils of gambling.
notes: 'asataś cārjanam': literally 'acquisition of what is not', i.e. of unreal or illusory wealth (winnings not truly one's own); the exact sense is left open. 'vipratipatti' here = loss, going astray.

words.gloss: removal of phlegm, bile, fat and sweat
in situations of anger and fear

hindi: मृगया में तो व्यायाम होता है, कफ, पित्त, मेद और पसीने का नाश होता है, चलते और स्थिर शरीर पर लक्ष्य-भेद का अभ्यास होता है, क्रोध और भय की स्थितियों में पशुओं के चित्त का ज्ञान होता है, और यात्रा सदा नहीं करनी पड़ती — ऐसा।
english: In hunting, on the other hand, there is exercise, removal of phlegm, bile, fat and sweat, practice at the target on a moving and on a standing body, knowledge of the minds of animals in situations of anger and fear, and marching that is not constant. So (runs the view).
notes: 'anitya-yānam' is ambiguous: 'marching only occasionally' (hunting takes one out only now and then) or 'movement that is not fixed, irregular'; rendered literally. 'cale sthite ca kāye' = on a moving and on a still body (of the quarry).

words.gloss: between the vices of gambling and women

hindi: "द्यूत और स्त्री के व्यसनों में द्यूत का व्यसन अधिक भारी है" — ऐसा कौणपदन्त कहते हैं।
english: "Between the vices of gambling and women, the vice of gambling (is the more serious)," says Kaunapadanta.
notes: The predicate 'is the more serious' is not in the line; it is carried over from 'garīyasī' in 39, as in all these comparisons.

hindi: "क्योंकि जुआरी निरन्तर, रात में दीपक के प्रकाश में, और माता के मर जाने पर भी, जुआ खेलता ही रहता है;
english: "For the gambler keeps gambling continuously, at night by lamplight, and even when his mother has died;
notes: 'mātari ca mṛtāyām' is a locative absolute: 'even when the mother is dead'.

hindi: और कठिनाई में पूछे जाने पर वह क्रोध करता है।
english: and when questioned in a difficulty, he gets angry.

words.gloss: at the places of bathing, toilet and meals

hindi: स्त्री-व्यसन में तो स्नान, शृंगार और भोजन के स्थानों पर धर्म और अर्थ के विषय में पूछताछ होती ही रहती है।
english: In the vice of women, on the other hand, inquiry into dharma and wealth does take place at the places of bathing, toilet and meals.
notes: 'pratikarma' = toilet, adornment of the body. 'bhūmi' = place or occasion.

words.gloss: to get rid of (lit. to drain away)

hindi: और स्त्री को राजा के हित में नियुक्त किया जा सकता है, या गुप्त दण्ड से अथवा रोग से हटाया जा सकता है या निकाल दिया जा सकता है" — ऐसा कहा गया है।
english: And a woman can be employed in the king's interest, or be turned away or got rid of by secret punishment or by disease." So it is said.
notes: The e-text's '.' in 'rājahite.niyoktum' joins two separate words (a locative and an infinitive), not compound members; the printed text has sandhi there. 'avasrāvayitum' (causative of ava-√sru, 'to make flow off') = to get rid of; sense slightly uncertain.

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.

words.gloss: having something that can be won back
having nothing that can be won back

hindi: द्यूत में हारा हुआ वापस लिया जा सकता है; स्त्री-व्यसन में वापस लेने योग्य कुछ नहीं होता।
english: Gambling has something that can be won back; the vice of women has nothing that can be won back.

hindi: दर्शन न देना, कार्य से विरक्ति, समय बीत जाने से अनर्थ और धर्म की हानि, शासन की दुर्बलता, और पान का अनुबन्ध — ये हैं।
english: Not appearing (in public), aversion to work, loss and loss of dharma through letting time pass, weakness of the administration, and addiction to drink: these (are the evils of the vice of women).
notes: The subject 'evils of the vice of women' is implied by 53; the list is Kautilya's answer. 'tantra' = the administration, the machinery of state.

words.gloss: between the vices of women and drink

hindi: "स्त्री और पान के व्यसनों में स्त्री-व्यसन अधिक भारी है" — ऐसा वातव्याधि कहते हैं।
english: "Between the vices of women and drink, the vice of women (is the more serious)," says Vatavyadhi.
notes: Predicate supplied from 39 as in 47.

hindi: "क्योंकि स्त्रियों के विषय में अनेक प्रकार की मूर्खता 'निशान्त-प्रणिधि' में समझाई जा चुकी है।
english: "For folly of many kinds in regard to women has been explained in 'Conduct in the inner apartments' (niśānta-praṇidhi).
notes: 'niśānta-praṇidhi' (niśānta = the inner apartments, the royal residence; praṇidhi = arrangement, conduct) is a reference to an earlier section of the work bearing that title; the line says only that the matter was explained there.

words.gloss: removal of the fatigue of work

hindi: पान में तो शब्द आदि इन्द्रिय-विषयों का उपभोग, प्रीति से दान, परिजनों का सम्मान, और कार्य के श्रम का नाश होता है" — ऐसा कहा गया है।
english: In drinking, on the other hand, there is enjoyment of the sense-objects, sound and the rest, giving out of affection, honouring of attendants, and removal of the fatigue of work." So it is said.

hindi: "नहीं" — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.

words.gloss: in the case of wives within (the household)
in the case of those not to be approached

hindi: स्त्री-व्यसन में अन्तःपुर की स्त्रियों से सन्तान की उत्पत्ति और आत्म-रक्षा होती है; बाहरी स्त्रियों से इसके विपरीत होता है; और अगम्या स्त्रियों से सर्वनाश होता है।
english: In the vice of women there is birth of offspring and protection of oneself in the case of wives within (the household); the opposite in the case of outside women; and complete ruin in the case of those who must not be approached.
notes: 'antar-dāreṣu' = wives inside, i.e. the king's own wives of the inner apartments; 'bāhyeṣu' = women outside that; 'agamyeṣu' = women forbidden to approach. 'viparyayaḥ' = the reverse of the two benefits just named.

hindi: वे दोनों पान-व्यसन में होते हैं।
english: Both of those are (found) in the vice of drink.
notes: 'both' = the opposite (of the benefits) and complete ruin, from 59.

words.gloss: loss of learning, intelligence, life, wealth and friends
in skills of lute and song

hindi: पान की सम्पत् यह है — संज्ञा का नाश, पागल न होने पर भी पागलपन, मरा न होने पर भी मृतक जैसी दशा, गुप्तांगों का दिखना, श्रुत, प्रज्ञा, प्राण, धन और मित्रों की हानि, सज्जनों से वियोग, अनर्थकारी लोगों से संयोग, तथा धन का नाश करने वाले वीणा और गीत के कौशलों में आसक्ति।
english: The excellence of drink (is): loss of consciousness, madness of one who is not mad, the state of a corpse of one who is not dead, exposure of the private parts, loss of learning, intelligence, life, wealth and friends, separation from the good, association with the worthless, and addiction to skills of lute and song, which destroy wealth.
notes: 'pāna-sampat' is said with irony: the 'excellence' of drink is a list of evils; rendered with the glossary's fixed 'excellence'. The e-text writes 'samyogas' and 'sampat' with m for the anusvāra; not flagged. 'anarthya' = useless, worthless (persons or things).

hindi: द्यूत और मद्य में द्यूत अधिक भारी है।
english: Between gambling and liquor, gambling (is the more serious).
notes: Predicate supplied from 39 as in 47 and 55.

words.gloss: for the sake of a stake

hindi: किसी एक पक्ष की, दाँव के कारण होने वाली जीत या हार — चाहे प्राणियों पर हो या निर्जीव वस्तुओं पर — दो पक्षों के विभाजन से प्रकृतियों में कोप उत्पन्न करती है।
english: The victory or defeat of one side, for the sake of a stake, whether (in play) with living creatures or with inanimate things, causes anger among the constituent elements through the division into two parties.
notes: 'ekeṣām' = of some, of one of the two parties. 'prāṇiṣu niścetaneṣu vā' = games played with animals (fights, races) or with lifeless objects (dice); the text itself only says 'living' and 'without consciousness'. 'prakṛti' rendered per the glossary.

words.gloss: having the nature of a confederacy
because of weakness of the administration

hindi: और विशेष रूप से संघों में तथा संघ-धर्म वाले राजकुलों में द्यूत के कारण भेद और उसके कारण विनाश होता है; इसलिए असत् का प्रग्रह, शासन की दुर्बलता के कारण, व्यसनों में सबसे पापपूर्ण है — ऐसा।
english: And especially among confederacies and among royal families that have the nature of a confederacy, there is division caused by gambling, and destruction caused by that; therefore indulgence of the bad is the most sinful of vices, because of (its causing) weakness of the administration. So (ends the argument).
notes: 'asat-pragraha' (favouring, indulging what is bad) here refers to gambling, which the verse 65 generalises as desire; it could also be read as 'favouring of bad persons'. 'pāpiṣṭhatama' is a double superlative (pāpiṣṭha + -tama).

words.gloss: because of the abundance of evils

hindi: असत् का प्रग्रह काम है और सत् का अवग्रह क्रोध; दोषों की बहुलता के कारण ये दोनों अत्यन्त व्यसन माने गए हैं।
english: Desire is the favouring of the bad, and anger is the restraining of the good; because of the abundance of their evils both are considered extreme vices.
notes: 'asatām' and 'satām' may be masculine (bad/good persons) or neuter (bad/good things); the verse plays on both. Both half-lines have 16 syllables (śloka).

hindi: इसलिए आत्मवान्, वृद्धों की सेवा करने वाला और जितेन्द्रिय व्यक्ति, मूल को नष्ट करने वाले, व्यसनों के आरम्भ-रूप क्रोध और काम को त्याग दे।
english: Therefore the self-possessed one, who attends on the elders and has conquered his senses, should give up anger and desire, the starting-point of vices, which destroy the root.
notes: 'vyasana-ārambham' and 'mūla-haram' are singular accusatives qualifying each of 'kopam' and 'kāmam'. 'mūla' = the root (of prosperity, of the kingdom) is not specified by the line. Both half-lines have 16 syllables.
